skeleton.description: Multi-model code review pipeline: parallel first-pass review, bounded debate rounds, merged findings with consensus tags, and a Markdown report.

state.name: ingest
state.contract:
Read the file at config.diff (a unified git diff in plain text).
Gate logic — return TRIVIAL (set data.trivial_reason to a descriptive string) if ANY of: • the file is empty or contains no +/- content lines • every changed file matches a trivial pattern: lockfiles → package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, *.lock, go.sum, go.lock generated → dist/*, build/*, *.min.js, *.generated.*, vendor/*, __generated__/* binary → file header contains "Binary files" (git binary diff marker)
Return ERROR if config.models has fewer than 2 entries (set data.error_reason accordingly).
Otherwise return PROCEED and write to output dir: • diff.txt — the raw diff text verbatim • file_manifest.json — JSON array of changed file paths extracted from the diff headers (lines starting with "diff --git a/…")

state.name: trivial_exit
state.contract: Read data.trivial_reason and config.models. Write to output dir: • findings.json — empty JSON array [] • report.md — minimal Markdown: # Code Review — No Substantive Changes <blank line> <data.trivial_reason> <blank line> --- Models: <config.models joined by ", "> | Rounds: 0 Return DONE.

state.name: chunk
state.contract:
Read diff.txt from the ingest stage output.
Parse the unified diff into per-file sections (split on "diff --git" headers). For each file section: • If the section is ≤ 30 000 characters, emit it as a single chunk. • If it exceeds 30 000 characters, split by hunk boundary ("@@ … @@") into sub-chunks, each ≤ 30 000 characters. Mark every sub-chunk is_partial = true. • If a single hunk exceeds 30 000 characters, record the file in the skipped list (no chunk emitted for that file) with reason "single hunk exceeds context limit".
Pair every chunk with config.context (may be empty string) to form enriched review units.
Write to output dir: • chunks.json — JSON array of { chunk_id (string), file (string), hunk_index (number), content (string), context (string), is_partial (boolean) } • skipped_files.json — JSON array of { file (string), reason (string) }; empty array if none.
Set data.chunk_count to the total number of chunks produced (integer). Return DONE.

state.name: prepare
state.contract: Read config.models (array of model-identifier strings). Set data.model_list to an array of objects in the same order: [ { model: config.models[0] }, { model: config.models[1] }, … ] Return DONE.

state.name: reviewer
state.contract:
You are an expert code reviewer. You receive: branchInput.model — your model identifier (already wired as your runtime model) branchIndex — your 0-based position in the model list
Read chunks.json from the chunk stage output. Review every chunk.
Rules: • Only cite files that appear in chunks.json — do NOT invent file names. • Only cite line numbers that exist within the chunk's +/- diff lines. • Severity must be one of: critical, high, medium, low, nit — no other values. • Category must be one of: bug, security, performance, style, correctness, readability, maintainability.
Write findings.json to YOUR output directory: JSON array of zero or more objects, each with exactly: { file: string, line_range: [start, end], severity: string, category: string, comment: string } An empty array [] is valid if you find no issues.

state.name: merge_first
state.contract:
Read findings.json from every reviewer branch output directory (one dir per branch). For each branch directory, if findings.json is missing or unparseable, record that branch's model identifier (data.model_list[branchIndex].model) in data.failed_models (array of model-identifier strings; default []).
Collect all valid findings. Build a deduplication key per finding: key = file + "::" + JSON.stringify(line_range) + "::" + category
Merge findings that share the same key into one entry: • models: array of model identifiers that raised this finding (no duplicates) • comment: take the comment from the highest-severity model's finding, or the first • severity: take the most severe across duplicates; normalise to critical/high/medium/low/nit
Write merged_findings.json to output dir: JSON array of { file, line_range, severity, category, comment, models }
Set data.failed_models (may be []). Return DONE.

state.name: debater
state.contract:
You are a code reviewer in a structured multi-model debate. You receive: branchInput.model — your model identifier (already wired as your runtime model) branchIndex — your 0-based position in the model list data.iteration — the 0-based debate round counter
Read the current merged findings: • If data.iteration == 0 (first debate round), read merged_findings.json from the merge_first stage output. • Otherwise read merged_findings.json from the tally_debate stage output (most recent iteration). The runtime injects both upstream directories.
SKIP all nit-level findings — treat them as already settled; do not debate them.
For each non-nit finding, decide ONE action: "confirm" — you agree this is a genuine issue "retract" — you believe this finding is wrong or out of scope (give reason) "challenge" — you dispute another model's finding (give specific reason) "add" — a new issue not yet in the merged list (provide full finding object)
Write debate_updates.json to YOUR output directory: JSON array of zero or more objects: { finding_key: string (file + "::" + JSON.stringify(line_range) + "::" + category), action: string ("confirm" | "retract" | "challenge" | "add"), reason: string, new_finding: object? (only for action="add"; same schema as first-pass findings) } An empty array [] is valid if you agree with everything.

state.name: tally_debate
state.contract:
Read debate_updates.json from every debater branch output directory (one dir per branch). Read the current merged findings (merged_findings.json) from the most recent upstream merge stage (merge_first for iteration 0, previous tally_debate output for later iterations).
Apply all updates to the findings set: • "retract": remove the issuing model from that finding's models array. If models becomes empty, remove the finding entirely. • "add": insert new finding; if key already exists merge models arrays. • "confirm" / "challenge": no structural change (record counts only for convergence check).
After applying: re-deduplicate by key and re-normalise severity (critical/high/medium/low/nit).
Write merged_findings.json to output dir (updated findings set).
Convergence: set data.debate_converged = true if EITHER: (a) this round produced zero retractions AND zero new additions, OR (b) data.iteration + 1 >= config.debate_rounds Otherwise leave data.debate_converged false (or unset).
Return DONE.

state.name: tag_consensus
state.contract:
Determine the source of final merged findings: • If the debate loop ran (tally_debate output exists), read merged_findings.json from the tally_debate stage output. • Otherwise (check_debate routed here directly) read merged_findings.json from the merge_first stage output.
Compute total_models = config.models.length - (data.failed_models ? data.failed_models.length : 0).
For each finding add a consensus field: "agreed" if finding.models.length === total_models "majority" if finding.models.length > total_models / 2 "contested" otherwise
Write tagged_findings.json to output dir: JSON array of findings with all fields (file, line_range, severity, category, comment, models, consensus).
Set data.rounds_completed = (data.debate_converged !== undefined ? data.iteration + 1 : 0). Return DONE.

state.name: synthesize
state.contract:
Read tagged_findings.json from the tag_consensus stage output. Read skipped_files.json from the chunk stage output. Read file_manifest.json from the ingest stage output.
Validation before writing: • Drop any finding whose file is NOT in file_manifest.json (guards against hallucinated files). • Ensure every finding's severity is one of critical/high/medium/low/nit; drop findings with invalid severity.
Write to YOUR output directory:
── findings.json ── Clean JSON array; every element has EXACTLY these fields (no extras): file (string), line_range ([start, end] integers), severity (critical|high|medium|low|nit), category (string), comment (string), models (array of model-identifier strings), consensus (agreed|majority|contested)
── report.md ── A valid Markdown document with this structure:
1. "## Executive Summary" section containing: - Table or bullet list: finding counts by severity (critical/high/medium/low/nit) - Finding counts by consensus level (agreed/majority/contested) - "**Models used:**" list from config.models - "**Debate rounds completed:**" data.rounds_completed - "**Failed models:**" data.failed_models (omit line if empty)
2. One "## <filename>" section per changed file that has findings, sorted so files with higher-severity findings appear first. Within each file section, findings are sorted severity-descending. Each finding is rendered as a bullet: `- [SEVERITY] L<start>–<end> · <category>: <comment>` where SEVERITY badge is one of [CRITICAL] [HIGH] [MEDIUM] [LOW] [NIT].
3. "## Files Skipped / Partially Reviewed" section (omit if skipped_files.json is empty), listing each entry from skipped_files.json with a ⚠ warning.
4. Horizontal rule footer: `---` `Models: <config.models joined> | Rounds: <data.rounds_completed>`
Do NOT include inline diff snippets. Write no files other than findings.json and report.md.
